thread:
anya: autoscaler alert popped for us-west1-b: opaque quota violation when allocating n1-gpu nodes, lots of pods stuck Pending with `0/` nodes schedulable. saw repeated 'Insufficient ephemerals' and attach errors. anyone on call?
infra-bot: [alert] cluster=prod-west1, zone=us-west1-b, reason=GPU_QUOTA_REJECT, count=42, first_seen=2024-10-07T14:02:14Z
raj: thanks — I see the same. our regional quota for A100 in that zone is at limit. GCP returned RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED for nodepool create. autoscaler kept retrying and now backoff.
marta: impact: customer-facing latency spikes on long-run generation jobs routed to prod-west1. small percentage of requests failing over to fallback model in us-west1-c but capacity there is getting warmed.
kevin: can we force rehome pods to other clusters / nodepools? we have tolerations+nodeAffinity on the big batch jobs that prefer west1-b. quick idea: add a temporary lighter nodepool in west1-c (spot) and change deployment nodeSelector to allow it. cost will spike.
olivia: not ideal to mutate deploys. can we get autoscaler to target cross-cluster scheduling? currently routing is per-cluster, the request router only fails over when region-level capacity is exhausted.
raj: autoscaler can't create nodes in another cluster. we could: 1) create a new nodepool in prod-west1 cluster in us-west1-c with GPUs; 2) adjust deployment affinity via a rollout to relax zone preference; 3) use descheduler to evict noncritical pods to free GPUs.
anya: what's fastest? ops-approve for creating nodepool takes a few minutes (quota checks). If we patch the daemonset/affinity it might roll slow.
kevin: fastest: create ephemeral nodepool in us-west1-c with same labels, set --min=0 --max=10, taint it with gpu-ephemeral=true:NoSchedule and add toleration to the workloads by patching replicasets (one-line kubectl). then scale up the nodepool to 2 nodes.
marta: do we have spare regional quota? GCP quota is per-zone, but we have a small buffer in us-west1-c. I'll check right now.
sam: quick commands if we go ephemeral:
```
# create nodepool (gcloud example)
gcloud container node-pools create ephem-gpu-1 \
  --cluster=prod-west1 --zone=us-west1-c --machine-type=a2-highgpu-1g \
  --num-nodes=0 --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 \
  --tags=gpu-ephemeral --node-taints=gpu-ephemeral=true:NoSchedule
# then patch deployment to tolerate
gkg kubectl -n ml patch deploy big-batch -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"gpu-ephemeral","operator":"Equal","value":"true","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}}}'
# scale nodepool
gcloud container node-pools update ephem-gpu-1 --enable-autoscaling --min-nodes=0 --max-nodes=4 --zone=us-west1-c
```
infra-bot: quota-check: us-west1-c A100 available quota=3, requested pending=2 (approx).
raj: if we create ephemeral pool, please make sure the node taint is strict and we don't accidentally schedule non-gpu workloads. also add a kubelet label `redwood/ephemeral=true` to help identify.
anya: Marta, do you have ops rights to spin the pool?
marta: I requested ops-approval and got green. spinning up 1 node now.
olivia: parallel ask: should we tweak cluster-autoscaler flags to be more permissive about cross-zonal fallback? we have `--balance-similar-node-groups` on; maybe enable `--expander=random` to prefer faster groups. But that won't help across clusters.
kevin: long-term we should implement a global placement controller that can route GPU requests across clusters in the same region before failing over to CPU-only fallbacks. short-term, ephemeral pool + toleration patch looks quickest.
sam: note on rollback: add a label `temp-rehome=20241007` and a script to remove tolerations & nodepool after 6 hours. I'll prepare.
raj: monitoring: add a Grafana panel to show zone-level GPU quota and nodepool create failures (API error rates). set an alert for RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED >=3 in 5m.
anya: agreed. Also can we reduce batch job parallelism to lower burst needs until pool stabilizes? patching replicas to 50% for now.
marta: node came up, pods started scheduling to ephem-gpu-1, I see 6 pods moved. latency dropped for those jobs.
olivia: cost note: ephemeral spot nodes are cheaper but preemptible; keep critical jobs pinned to reserved capacity. we should also notify customers with long-running jobs if their tasks are bumped to spot.
kevin: action items:
- Marta: verify quota and leave pool autoscaling min=0 max=4 (done)
- Sam: cleanup script & label automation (in progress)
- Raj: add Grafana alert and dashboard row (in progress)
- Anya: throttle batch replicas to 50% until midnight PT (done)
- Olivia: draft post-incident note for product & cs (will do)

anya: thanks all — keeping this thread open for 1hr for followups. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: [resolved] alert auto-silenced by action 'ephemeral_pool_created' at 2024-10-07T14:10:34Z
kevin: big follow-up: we need a runbook for opaque quota errors that walks through ephemeral pool creation, toleration patch, and rollback. I'll draft and link here.
marta: created minimal runbook at https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/zonal-opaque-quota (draft). please review.
raj: nice. once runbook is in place, we can automate a safe fallback API that creates ephemeral pools and patches a deployment via the placement-controller with approvals.
olivia: also file a quota increase request for us-west1-b; ops: quota request #Q-2147.
anya: closing for now — re-open if we see RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED again.
